column1: # parser/spec/lex.tsv — the trivia-preserving lexer parity corpus.
# Exactly three tab-separated columns: escaped source, OK/ERR clean-EOF
# status, and the exact token stream as canonical JSON. Token `si` values are
# UTF-8 byte offsets. Every column uses the parser/spec escape notation.
# Both ports own independent strict readers and renderers; keep the exact
# row-count ratchets in those runners and parser/spec/README.md in sync.
# Adjacent string quotes are unconditional #TX boundaries, including after
# the slash that follows a completed receiver.
# § base-prefixed boundaries — the class a base-prefix arm in the
#   decimal-boundary matcher used to exist for. The two stock scanners
#   disagreed here until tabnas parser v0.8.3: before a `.`, Go called
#   `0xFF` a number and the TS port called it text (and separately, Go
#   accepted an uppercase `0XFF` marker where TS did not). Both are fixed
#   upstream, the arm is DELETED from both ports, and NUR.md §NUR061 records
#   THESE ROWS EARNED THE RETIREMENT — do not delete them. They pin the
#   classification the arm used to guarantee, so with the arm gone their
#   passing is what shows the stock scanners now agree; and they are the
#   regression pin if an upstream release ever slips back.
#   `0xFF.x` is deliberately kept as an AGREEING shape, labelled. The old
#   divergence depended on the follow character — the TS scanner decided the
#   run before the dot by looking PAST it, so `0xFF.5` and `0xFF.e5`
#   diverged while `0xFF.x` agreed. A sweep probing only an agreeing shape
#   would have called the arm dead while it was load-bearing; that is the
#   mistake this section exists to prevent, so one of each stays pinned.
